primary_title: G Protein-Coupled Receptor Kinase 3 and Protein Kinase C Phosphorylate the Distal C-Terminal Tail of the Chemokine Receptor CXCR4 and Mediate Recruitment of beta-Arrestin
decision_basis: Ser346/347 phosphosite and kinase perturbation evidence supports the bounded CXCR4-to-ARRB2 recruitment/desensitization edge.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the CXCR4 distal-tail site-set, CXCL12/pepducin and GRK3/PKC context; no exclusive universal mechanism, SCI or terminal-TF expansion.

primary_title: beta-Arrestin-2 interaction and internalization of the human P2Y1 receptor are dependent on C-terminal phosphorylation sites
decision_basis: P2Y1 Ser352/Thr358 mutant evidence supports the bounded site-set-to-ARRB2 recruitment/internalization edge.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human P2Y1, ADP and Ser352/Thr358 heterologous-cell context; no direct phosphopeptide-binding, universal physiology, SCI or terminal-TF expansion.

primary_title: Two serines in the distal C-terminus of the human beta1-adrenoceptor determine beta-arrestin2 recruitment
decision_basis: ADRB1 Ser461/Ser462 phosphosite and mutant evidence supports the bounded site-set-to-ARRB2 recruitment/internalization edge.
limitations_preserved: Preserve human ADRB1 Ser461/Ser462, agonist and HEK293/FRET context; no universal adrenergic mechanism, SCI or terminal-TF expansion.

primary_title: Differential desensitization, receptor phosphorylation, beta-arrestin recruitment, and ERK1/2 activation by the two endogenous ligands for the CC chemokine receptor 7
decision_basis: The cited primary supports the CCR7 T373-T376/S378 cluster as a CCL19-dependent phosphorylation/recruitment determinant with beta-arrestin2-dependent ERK output; this is distinct from the existing whole-receptor CCR7-ARRB2 edge.
limitations_preserved: Human CCR7/H9 and HEK293 contexts; CCL19 versus CCL21 ligand bias; cluster-level site-set rather than single-site proof; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

primary_title: Identification of a Ser/Thr cluster in the C-terminal domain of the human prostaglandin receptor EP4 that is essential for agonist-induced beta-arrestin1 recruitment but differs from the apparent principal phosphorylation site
decision_basis: The cited primary directly supports the EP4 S389/S390/T391/S392 recruitment cluster, distinct from the principal phosphorylation region, with internalization readout.
limitations_preserved: Human EP4 receptor and agonist mutant-system context; recruitment cluster versus principal phosphorylation region; no single-site exclusivity, SCI or terminal-TF inference.

primary_title: The sustainability of interactions between the orexin-1 receptor and beta-arrestin-2 is defined by a single C-terminal cluster of hydroxy amino acids and modulates the kinetics of ERK MAPK regulation
decision_basis: The cited primary directly supports the OX1R T418/S419/T421/T422 C1 cluster as a sustained beta-arrestin2 interaction determinant with ERK kinetics.
limitations_preserved: Human OX1R/HEK293T and mouse beta-arrestin-deficient MEF rescue contexts; cluster mutation does not abolish receptor internalization; no single-site exclusivity, SCI or terminal-TF inference.
